canonical_name: Mirsky's antichain-cover theorem for finite partially ordered sets (exact source and encoding open)
literal_source_claim_zh: 偏序集分解为反链的最小数目
literal_source_claim_en: The minimum number of antichains in a decomposition of a partially ordered set.
source_attribution: Leon Mirsky, 1971 (catalog metadata; primary bibliography identified)
candidate_family_not_credited_as_stateme: For a finite partially ordered set, the least cardinality of a family of antichains covering the full carrier equals the greatest cardinality of a chain; the partition form requires a checked cover-disjointization transport.
statement_blocker: The repository supplies no source locator, finite-carrier or nonempty premise, height convention, definition of decomposition, minimization encoding, ordered binders, boundary cases, or Lean expression. The strong 1971 primary bibliographic lead was inaccessible for theorem-text inspection. An inspected Coq source uses a possibly overlapping antichain cover on a finite inhabited carrier, so selecting a Finpartition, silently equating cover with partition, or choosing another height convention now would invent proposition-changing details.
target_decision: retain the standard finite-poset Mirsky theorem family at provisional H1 and require an independently reviewed immutable source passage before freezing one formal target

canonical_formal_target.candidate_expression: For a selected finite poset carrier, the minimum cardinality of a family covering the carrier whose members are IsAntichain under <= equals the maximum chain cardinality represented by Set.chainHeight; an exact partition form and an LTSeries step-length form are alternate candidates requiring checked transports.
